title: Machine Learning Algorithm Comparison
text: This was a research report where I got to choose a dataset on Kaggle and apply 4 classification algorithms to the dataset using Python. The dataset I chose was deepfake detection data that contained various features for the models to determine whether the media data was real or fake. Various pre-processing and exploratory data analysis steps were needed before applying the models. The results showed exceptional accuracy, but these results were reflective of the synthetic, balanced nature of the dataset rather than the model’s efficiency.

Libraries Used

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, StratifiedKFold, cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score,
    f1_score, roc_auc_score, confusion_matrix, classification_report
)

title: Machine Learning Algorithm Comparison
text:
Data Preprocessing
The dataset was loaded and cleaned by removing irrelevant columns. Categorical variables were encoded using a Label Encoder and the target label was converted to a binary format.

df = pd.read_excel('deepfake_detection_metadata_dataset.csv.xlsx')

df = df.drop(columns=['generation_method', 'media_id'])

categorical_cols = ['media_type', 'content_category', 'audio_present', 'source_platform']
le = LabelEncoder()
for col in categorical_cols:
    df[col] = le.fit_transform(df[col].astype(str))

df['label'] = (df['label'] == 'Fake').astype(int)

title: Machine Learning Algorithm Comparison
text:
Feature Selection & Train/Test Split
Nine features were selected based on their relevance to deepfake detection. The data was split 80/20 into training and test sets using stratified sampling to preserve class balance.

FEATURES = [
    'media_type', 'content_category', 'face_count', 'audio_present',
    'lip_sync_score', 'visual_artifacts_score', 'compression_level',
    'lighting_inconsistency_score', 'source_platform'
]

X = df[FEATURES]
y = df['label']

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y
)

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_scaled  = scaler.transform(X_test)

title: Machine Learning Algorithm Comparison
Machine Learning Algorithm Comparison
text:
Feature Importance
The Random Forest model was used to rank the importance of each feature in predicting whether media was real or fake.

rf_model = models['Random Forest']['model']
importances = pd.Series(rf_model.feature_importances_, index=FEATURES)
importances_sorted = importances.sort_values(ascending=False)

for feat, imp in importances_sorted.items():
    bar = '█' * int(imp * 50)
    print(f"  {feat:<35} {imp*100:5.2f}%  {bar}")

title: John McGrath
text:
My name is John McGrath, I am 22 years of age, from Dublin, and I am a final year business studies student in DCU, specialising in data analytics. I am due to graduate in October 2026 with a second-class honours degree.
I am hoping to begin my professional career working in the field of business analytics. Over the course of my studies, I developed a strong interest in this field. What began as an introduction to the topic in first and second year quickly grew into a passion for uncovering insights from raw data and using them to drive better business decisions.
During my degree, I was fortunate enough to partake in a full-year Erasmus programme, where I studied in the University of Porto’s School of Economics and Management for my third year. During my studies here, I was able to further develop my technical skills through modules like business analytics and information management, where I learned a number of valuable analytical skills. On top of academic progression, this experience helped to deepen my cultural understanding and appreciation and overall, it was hugely beneficial for my personal development.
Outside of university, my main passion is sports. I have been involved in sports for my whole life. I have tried many different sports over the years, and I currently play Gaelic Football and soccer, and I go to the gym. My love for sport is reflected in my current part-time job. I work for Experience Gaelic Games, where I teach tourists how to play football, hurling and handball. This is a unique opportunity, as I get to represent Irish culture and share it with people from all over the world.

text:
Data Analytics Skills
These are the technical skills I have learned in my time in university.




Python
Over the past year, I have gained a strong foundation in Python, gaining hands-on experience with core concepts, including the language basics, control flow through conditional statements and loops, and working with key data structures. This foundation will enable me to apply my skills effectively while continuing to develop further abilities.





SQL
I have developed a comprehensive understanding of SQL and the core skills required to work effectively with relational databases. This includes the ability to design and interpret ERDs, create databases and tables, and write queries using a range of join clauses to retrieve and manipulate data across multiple tables.





PowerBI
Power BI has helped me to develop a strong understanding of data visualisation. It helped me learn the necessary skills to turn raw data into clear, understandable insights. This includes building interactive dashboards and reports, and applying visualisation best practices to present data in a way that is both accessible and impactful.





Excel
Having worked with Excel since my first year, I have developed a strong proficiency in the application over time. This experience has given me a thorough command of its core features, including data organisation, formulas, functions, and charting, as well as more advanced capabilities such as pivot tables and data analysis tools.





Microsoft Access
I have developed a solid understanding of Microsoft Access and its role as a relational database management tool. This includes creating and managing databases, designing tables and defining relationships between them, and building queries to extract and manipulate data.





R
Although this is an area I need to work on, I have developed a solid foundation in R, gaining experience in using it as a tool for analysis and data exploration. This includes working with data structures such as vectors, data frames, and lists.
